summary: Batch B, family B5 (`set_path`). Four conjecture-local helpers (X39, X11, X26 `xy_path` and X116 `ST_path`, the same body with its set parameters renamed) now unfold to `GTBase.walks_paths.seq_set_path X Y p`: `p` is a nonempty vertex sequence whose first entry is in `X` and last entry in `Y`, without repetition, with consecutive entries adjacent. Every helper had exactly that match, so all four are convertible. Upstream, `seq_set_path_upath` states it as coq-graph-theory's `upath x (last x q) q` on the tail after splitting off the head, with both endpoint memberships explicit, and `seq_set_path_nodes` gives one from any irredundant packaged path. No guard is added: a one-vertex path is valid exactly in `X :&: Y`, empty endpoint sets admit none, and there is no disjointness, distinct-endpoint, length or internal-avoidance premise.

Five statements are affected: X39, cross-module X40 (through X39's helpers), X116 (whose hitting clause also uses the path predicate directly), X11 and X26. Each area's certificate freezes this family's chains (k distant or anticomplete paths, the separators) with the frozen helpers; the vertex-support and pairwise-distance helpers migrated by family path-vertices (B1) stay live there by design. The natural predecessor (`k.-1`, `d.-1`), the distance conventions, the positivity guards and every quantifier order are unchanged.

Historical snapshots: B1 froze only the vertex-support chains of these rows, so its snapshots call the live path predicates; they are kept verbatim and documented below. `X39Original`, `X40Original`, `X116Original`, `X11Original` and `X26Original` freeze the five rows end to end over B1's frozen support/distance objects (listed as `b1-frozen`, with B1's certificates) and this family's frozen path predicates; this family's own partial snapshots are documented in B1's spec as later-family snapshots.

Kernel evidence, independent of this textual report: `Print All Dependencies` of the five frozen statements and the five originals contains no live helper or chain declaration of this family and not `seq_set_path`; the originals reach no live B1 alias and not `seq_vertices`; each live statement reaches `seq_set_path` and its alias (/srv/graph-theory-rocq/coordination/evidence/B5-set_path/print_all_dependencies_summary.txt, with the probe and the full output beside it).

No statement text, doc block, manifest row or leg state changes (checked below). The genuine whole-sequence paths (X126, X14, X23, X178), the endpoint-tail simple paths, the empty-allowed Hom path, U9's `spath` (no uniqueness, not repaired) and the multigraph and directed path contracts are separate families.

B26 (set-separator, 2026-10-03): the live `x39_separates_xy` and `x26_separates_xy` are now aliases of upstream `GraphTheory.core.connectivity.separator`, so the ten certificates of this family that reach them (the Legacy and Original separator certificates and the X39, X40 and X26 row certificates, Legacy and Original) are proved through `GTBase.set_separators.seq_separatorP` and a pointwise transport of the separator clause instead of by conversion, with every statement and frozen body unchanged. B1's corresponding certificates, called conversions in the notes below, changed in the same way.

The final B26 integration also registers the actual A22 balls.X39Original, X40Original and X26Original complete rows over raw B1 supports, B5 paths/separators and A22 balls. Earlier per-family copies and all their frozen bodies remain unchanged; the deepest existing A22 whole proofs explicitly reuse the adapted B5 separator bridges.

B27 (distant-paths, 2026-10-03): the live X39 / X116 distant-path wrappers are now aliases of GTBase.distant_paths, so five Original certificates of this family (the X39 and X116 existence Originals and the X39, X40 and X116 Original rows), whose frozen chains keep B1's disjointness conjunct, are proved through has_k_distant_set_pathsP and pointwise row transports instead of by conversion, with every statement and frozen body unchanged; the Legacy certificates and X26's remain as they were.
